Polls in Brazil close at 4pm ET. 🇧🇷

No one is expected to get >50% of the vote and win in the first round, so Lula’s margin is the key metric to watch. Here’s a scenario breakdown:

- If Lula wins the first round by 5%+, he will be the clear favorite in the runoff on October 25th and Brazilian stocks will be red tomorrow.

- If Lula wins by, call it, 2-4%, it suggests the runoff will be very close. The coin flip scenario most polls have been predicting recently.

- If Lula is only up by 1-2%, Bolsonaro will be the runoff favorite and Brazilian stocks will almost certainly be green at the open. Bolsonaro means closer US relations.

- If Bolsonaro shocks the polls and actually leads Lula in the first round, as we saw with Abelardo in Colombia, Brazilian equities will be limit up. $EWZ

tweets.text:
I’m rereading “The Rise and Fall of American Growth” and found this passage to be quite thought-provoking when it comes to AI. 

Will AI be looked back on by historians as a “Great Invention?” I think so! 

Will rising income inequality (or our attempts to resolve it) cancel it out (or worse)? I don’t know, but it’s looking like it will be front and center in the next election
——
This book is based on an important idea having innumerable implications:

“Economic growth is not a steady process that creates economic advance at a regular pace, century after century. Instead, progress occurs much more rapidly in some times than in others. There was virtually no economic growth for millennia until 1770, only slow growth in the transition century before 1870, remarkably rapid growth in the century ending in 1970, and slower growth since then. Our central thesis is that some inventions are more important than others, and that the revolutionary century after the Civil War was made possible by a unique clustering, in the late nineteenth century, of what we will call the
"Great Inventions."

However, any consideration of U.S. economic progress in the future must look beyond innovation to contemplate the headwinds that are blowing like a gale to slow down the vessel of progress. Chief among these headwinds is the rise of inequality that since 1970 has steadily directed an ever larger share of the fruits of the American growth machine to the top of the income distribution.”

Seems people are confused by point number 4

So the logic is: RHchain is customer acquisition tool. Current Robinhood users are already making money for Robinhood. 

If they let them to take their money FROM Robinhood proper to Robinhood Chain, what would be the benefit for the users? They can already trade crypto and stocks within Robinhood. 

Only thing they would come to RHchain for would be new memecoins, and they would lose money fast on them (remember memecoins are a EV- casino, unlike stocks). So these existing users RH already owns and spent money acquiring would lose money and become less valuable customers.

But crypto natives in Ethereum and Solana ecosystems that are bridging to RHchain are net new users for Robinhood who can either generate fees through RHchain or later be integrated with RH eco as it evolves.
